overview: A group runs its own copy of Civicsmith to investigate how a government is meeting its obligations. Members bring documents in with a record of where each came from. They ask questions and support each answer with passages from those documents. A project concludes a question on the support it accepts, and the concluded question becomes a finding. The group publishes its findings as a case, in editions.

Then the group decides what to do. From the first suspicion, a project can open an action plan: the matters it is about and how well each is shown, the options open to it (a records request, a complaint, a story, testimony, a filing through counsel, and so on), which it chooses and which it declines with a reason, and up to three scenarios with checkpoints the group judges. Choosing an option starts an action, addressed to an office, an outlet or an organisation, never a private person. The assistant may draft what is sent; a member approves it and sends it by their own hand. The group then tracks replies and deadlines and, for a breach, the seven-stage escalation until compliance is restored.

Three things run through all of it. The record always says what is not known and why. It keeps track of who looked where and what they found. And the assistant finds, proposes and drafts, but a person makes every judgement and takes every act that commits the group.

otherRulings.title: A project's stage and its cases' readiness
otherRulings.decided: 'Closed' is the owner's recorded act with its judged reason; the other three stages are always computed. Each readiness rung shows by its own evidence; a published case reads Distributed, never Draft ('newspapers don't publish drafts'); Internally checked and Externally compliant read 'not yet evaluated' until the evaluations exist.

otherRulings.title: What a member reads when an act is refused
otherRulings.decided: A refused act shows the standard sentence first, then the act's own next step or alternative, as part of what the member reads, never a hidden field; every refusal that shares a code follows this pattern.

otherRulings.title: Thirteen points on presenting and resolving a contradiction
otherRulings.decided: An undetermined candidate is a lead; a record duty binds the joined members of every project drawing on either side until resolved; two projects' different conclusions are plurality, each attributed, unless they cannot both hold in the same respect; the question's own conclusion resolves a contradiction inquiry; the machine recommends only which respects may differ; a stale side moves nothing by itself; a hypothesised cause is published as 'cause not established'; an irreconcilable conclusion is disclosed; publication discloses, never blocks; accepting keeps the machine's reason the machine's; 'one of them is wrong' needs a written reason; a dismissal gives one fixed reason.

otherRulings.title: A conflict with a record the member cannot see
otherRulings.decided: Each project in such a conflict is told of it on its own side only, where it sits in that project, never the other project, its members or its side. Each notice lets the project ask to resolve it; when every project holding a side has asked, the projects are named to each other's members, names only. Members then respond to the notices; a response is relayed with only what the responder chose to share, their cover or an email ('stated, not verified') if they wish, none of it required. There is no discussion thread and no general messaging. A conflict that remains at publication is told to the publisher in the ceremony and highlighted in the published case, which never names the hidden record or who holds it.
otherRulings.src: DECISIONS.md DEC-85; K455, K456, K459; contradiction R49-R55

otherRulings.title: Sources, self-registered keys and doorbell material
otherRulings.decided: A source's dated, attributed disclosure history has its own home, seen only by those allowed and every read logged. A member registers their own browser-held signing key, made on their own device and confirmed by passphrase or device unlock at each use; every administrator is told and can revoke it. Doorbell material is graded received, not fetched: its chain of custody is the knock's receipt. A pseudonym is an identity detail, so a case says 'an unnamed source' unless the source consented, by their knocker secret or through a member's evidenced record. Hand-carried material follows a recorded rule and is taken in with the upload redesign.
otherRulings.src: build/rulings.md K509; sources R1-R15; membership R89-R91; provenance R51

otherRulings.title: The Action layer's shape
otherRulings.decided: The Action layer has an action plan: a member creates it, the system suggests options, and the member chooses and lays them out; it is not project management. There is no catalogue of response options and no budgets. One plan may address several related matters, and one option may serve several. A plan may start from a compliant or unclear determination, or open as soon as an inquiry begins. Lobbying is an option only to enforce or restore an existing requirement. An unticked option is undecided; declining is an optional act with a reason. A plan holds up to three scenarios. Options fall into mitigation, legal, awareness, journalistic, grassroots or other.
otherRulings.src: build/rulings.md K590 (rulings 1-10), K608 (1); docs/architecture/BIO_Action_v0_1.md §3, §4 rules 3, 4, 8, 9; build/plan/action-design/HANDOFF.md 'What Bob ruled'

otherRulings.title: Who and what an action may address, and who drafts
otherRulings.decided: An action is addressed to a government office by role and body, a reporter or outlet, an organisation or another civic group by role and organisation, or a described audience; never a private individual, and a breach action is addressed to an office (D1). The assistant drafts communications as proposals a member adopts (D2). An action may resolve as 'completed' when no counterparty's answer decides it, its own outcome saying what happened (D3). A project may declare its kind of work (reporting, fixing, legal, oversight, other), which shapes the assistant's suggestions and nothing else (D4). A started option may name the group's contact, which grants nothing (D5). Any group may use Civicsmith; a group with a stake in a matter discloses it (D6).
otherRulings.src: build/rulings.md K590 (D1-D6), K608 (1); docs/architecture/BIO_Action_v0_1.md §4 rules 6, 9, 10; actions R7, R9, R45; action-plans R21; filings R23

otherRulings.title: A plan closes only by a member, with a reason
otherRulings.decided: A member closes a plan with a reason; a plan never closes itself. A closed plan stays readable, and its subjects are free to join another plan.
otherRulings.src: action-plans R20; build/rulings.md K590; build/plan/action-design/HANDOFF.md 'What Bob ruled'

otherRulings.title: Acting on an unestablished premise
otherRulings.decided: An action that asserts a breach is refused by default unless it rests on a live noncompliant determination. A member may proceed anyway, openly, by an attributed act with a stated reason; the action and every filing, counsel packet and communication prepared from it then say first that it rests on an unestablished premise, with the reason, who and when. An action that seeks evidence, such as a records request or a request for comment, is never gated, and an overridden action never joins an escalation. A plan may rest on premises not yet established, shown as hunch debt.
otherRulings.src: docs/architecture/BIO_Action_v0_1.md §4 rule 2, §7 point 2, §8; build/rulings.md K600 (a), K608 (1); actions R8; filings R24; escalation R23

otherRulings.title: The venue sets the standard of evidence
otherRulings.decided: No action is refused for its evidence grade. Every filing and counsel packet shows each exhibit's grade and whether it is co-attested; where the jurisdiction profile states a venue's standard of evidence, it is shown beside them, and a grade the opposition could contest is flagged so counsel and members can prepare. Grade A is the highest grade the product offers: a ceiling, not a minimum.
otherRulings.src: docs/architecture/BIO_Action_v0_1.md §4 rule 13, §7 point 3; build/rulings.md K597 (3), K600 (b), K608 (1); filings R25; jurisdictions R39

otherRulings.title: Good faith hoped for, opposition prepared for
otherRulings.decided: People are presumed to want better outcomes, and a bad actor is identified by evidence, never by role. The system is nonetheless prepared for opposition: every plan is checked for a branch that answers a hostile response; pressure against the group or its supporters is recorded as evidence and can open an inquiry; and what counsel or another group needs to carry a matter on survives the group's disruption.
otherRulings.src: docs/architecture/BIO_Action_v0_1.md §4 rule 12, §7 point 1; build/rulings.md K597 (1), K608 (1); action-plans R19; actions R48

otherRulings.title: Deferred: licensed certification and joint action with other groups
otherRulings.decided: Certification of an output by a licensed professional is deferred; it comes back when a group needs a licensed name on an output, and meanwhile the attribution levels serve. Joint action with another group is recorded and deferred, including the near-term support described for it; it comes back when a coalition of groups asks to act jointly.

otherRulings.title: The old interface, and when a release is cut
otherRulings.decided: The old interface (civicos-ui/app.html) stays as it is, untested and unworked, until the new interface replaces it: in Bob's words, "You can leave the old interface, as it's not currently being worked on or tested, and will be replaced by the new interface once its design has evolved sufficiently". No release is cut until he says so ("releases aren't being cut until I say that we're ready to do one"), so what is built reaches a group's copy only then.

otherRulings.title: The assistant's planning suggestions
otherRulings.decided: Only a joined member starts a planning run, one plan at a time, never automatically. "Rather than a hard limit of 5 suggestions, the feature should present the best first 5. But also provide a means for the member to ask to see the next 'tranche' of 5 options, and so on": the tray shows the five strongest first and the member asks for the next five until none remain, with no score shown. The run drafts no letters, reads only the same project's earlier plans, and may plan for suspected matters, flagged by the plan's checks. The machine-work disclosure stops at adoption: the adopted option keeps it, the action and what is sent do not, and the record keeps who adopted it, from which run and when. It is switched on as soon as development can properly support it ("No legit reason I can think of not to switch it on as soon as development can properly support it").
